comment: A quick hike to kill some time. Trail is predominantly dry with a couple of puddles along the way.
Think about the spots you’d like to see and plan around it.
good place to go and pretty easy for beginner as it's not too steep. We came a day after rain and the trail looks pretty good still, not a lot of mud area.
Definitely would recommend sturdy shoes and bug spray. On weekends the main loop is pretty busy so make sure to book ahead

Great! One of my favourites. A great day trip ~1.5 hours out of Toronto. Ran into a group of hikers who almost skipped the cliff descent, don't forget to check those out!

Great location to hike close to the city.  Must book online (up to 5 days early) for parking pass.  We got there around 10am and the parking lot was almost empty, a few people at the beginning of the path but afterwards it was pretty empty.  Trails were well marked with lots of options to hike.  The caves/cliff aren’t as big as we expected, walk down the stairs to a small area that’s maybe 50m to walk and read a few signs on how they where created and then you turn around and go back the same way! But overall it would be a place I hike again!
Beautiful day beautiful trail
Nice gentle trail. Gets busy in the afternoon, recommend coming early.
Really nice trail abit muddy for the first 1km but after that it’s fully dry
Some parts of the trail were slippery and muddy due to melting ice.

You need to purchase a parking pass to get through the gate. 
The trail is super icy. Super super slippery. Bring cleats. 
Busy on the trail given the weather conditions. Friendly people views were meh for the hype.

A tough-ish walk in snowy conditions, but an enjoyable one. Variety of terrain with rewarding views points. Didn’t bump into anyone else on the trail. Well marked. Easy to get to. (Bonus, great brewery with delicious post-hike snacks about 3kms from the parking lot - Mono Centre Brewing)
A little icy but had a great hike and not crowded.
The trail is beautiful in the winter, but the washrooms are some of the most disgusting and putrid washrooms I've ever smelled.

Nice variety for all skill level. Some steep climbs and also some long, wide trails under tall tree canopies. Ponds and cliffs, crevices and changing forests (birch, sumac, pine, cedar), makes for a visually pleasing wander.
Great trail with lots of options
Whole trail is beautiful. Cliffs, Caves and ponds what more could you ask for!
Well marked and well maintained trails. Per.it has to be booked online, no option to buy at the park. Amazing trail overall, lots of different loops and side trails.

5 stars despite the rather horrific bathroom situation. The views are too good on this trail to give it any fewer stars. Make sure to book your pass ahead as well if you go, because the parking lot will probably be full!

Definitely a beautiful trail with lots of places to gear off the trail.
Great trail with a little bit of everything you'd want in a hike!

Eat Apples

Trail was good but some garbage need to be removed! Need more garbage cans.

I found it a little crowded so switched from the main trail to some side trails, overall it was a really nice park great views, the bathrooms were in rough shape in terms of cleanliness, and unfortunately, some of the visitors seem to be leaving trash behind on the trails.  It was a nice variety of forest and clearing the cliffs are very nice views and there lots of wild raspberries in some sections.

Mono Cliffs requires a reservation for parking and use of the park. Parking is easy to find and washrooms are located beside the lot at the trailhead. Another washroom is located further into the park. Cycling, dog and horseback friendly. The park offers great views with well marked trails, there is maps located all throughout the park to assist with navigation. There are many trails to chose from including a small portion of the Bruce trail, with many connecting together allowing for a custom route through the park.
Nice day to get out. Pretty hike.

Beautiful cliff side trail
Gorgeous day, no bugs, lots of people but a few really great spots on the trail where we were solitary

Amazing Area beautiful rock face views we definitely enjoyed. It would be good to have more picnic tables at the lookout.

Beautiful trail! You get to experience so many different landscapes throughout the hike, with birch, cedar and willow trees, rock cliff faces covered in soft moss, and opportunities to move from trail to trail at different points. Can’t wait to go back and see everything in full bloom.

In general, the trail is lovely, and the fall colours are great (although the leaves are already falling, so it might change in a few days).
We found the southern half of the loop to be less interesting. It mainly goes through the forest, and also goes through a lake which was nice but not particularly beautiful. If you are short on time, you can definitely skip it. 
Certainly don't miss the viewpoint, at least in the fall season (some trails that are suggested here on Alltrails don't go through it)!
Continue north from the viewpoint (on the Cliff-Top Side Trail), you will soon see stairs to your right, go down the stairs to see interesting rock formations in the cliff.
Continue with the trail north, not long after the stairs you will see an intersection. I recommend going right to the Walter Tovell Trail. This will take you to a very nice lake. 
Keep going on the Walter Tovell Trail until you reach another intersection. Take left to the Link Trail, which will take you to another nice lake.
From there you can go back to the parking lot.

Gorgeous walk through Mono Cliffs Park!  You can pre pay your parking and register online via 
https://reservations.ontarioparks.com/
For either an all day pass or a 4 hour vehicle permit for $7. 

We arrived on a Friday morning, and shared the park with a small handful of people. Walked the Cliff-Top Side Trail via Carriage Trail and Spillway Trail from the parking lot, we missed the turnoff at the pond that brings you into the forest. It was a hot and long walk on an open trail until we reached the forest and up a hill into the tree cover along the ridge.  Good idea to bring bug spray, good hiking shoes (there are rocks, different elevations plus stairs) don't forget water and snacks! The view of the Rock Cliffs (Jacob's Ladder) is magical, we thankfully had a moment to enjoy it without anyone else there, it is a small section of the walk on a deadend boardwalk that would easily get crowded. Breathtaking view a top of the cliffs from the look out platform. Overall a beautiful, lush, slice of the Bruce Trail, Niagara Escartment and Biosphere Reserve.

We went to check it out as we were in the area (my Mom recommended it as she had gone years back), only to discover you have to reserve a spot on the weekends. No cell reception in the area so we had to turn back down the road to get a signal to reserve a spot and pay and come back lol. Went to the viewing platform but I've seen nicer lookout spots for free tbh, would be nicer in the fall but Idk if it's worth it to look at a bunch of trees. Thought it would be a bit more scenic. If I could have a do over I'd check out other trails there instead of the cliff top trail. Based on other people's reviews there are nicer views.

This is a beautiful trail :) My husband and I took our 4 year old and 1 year old. My 4 year old walked the whole way on his own and my 1 year old was in a carrier. As we hiked up to the top there were a couple of steep spots, but nothing overly challenging. I was more than capable of navigating the whole trail and staircases with the carrier on. We only passed by two other people and the trails were well marked. Some graffiti on the posted trail maps makes them challenging to read so we used the map on our phone instead. Our main purpose of coming to this trail was to see “Jacob’s Ladder”. It was a beautiful spot with the boardwalk in between the narrow cliffs. Well worth it for us and it was a great way to spend an evening.

Dog friendly trail. I wouldn’t quite rate it as moderate. Fun trail. Completed in 2.5 hours with a few stops to enjoy the views.
a great wintery hike! not too strenuous and currently not icy, but lots of fresh snow! good for a leisurely dog walk or walk with the kids. be careful on the staircases.
Not a challenging hike but quite scenic during fall time with some informative signs about the land formations and cliffs.
Great trail. Markers well laid out to go between the different loops. So quiet and serene.
So gorgeous

A little boring in sections (as expected of Ontario) but the stairs leading down the cliffs is really cool! Definitely do not miss it (a few groups were skipping it as the stairs seem like they lead to nowhere). Trails are not very well marked and all become white marker after they converge. But all the trails head in a general loop so it was fine. There were not too many bugs on the day that I went in late May. Would come again!
Beautiful trail! Would agree that it’s moderate in difficulty. Definitely still muddy and icy in spots so wear waterproof hiking boots. View from the top is great and well worth the winding hike up!

Hiked with family, total ten people, with four teenagers. Everyone had a good time. It was drizzling a bit, other than that, all was perfect. Some parts were quite steep and slippery, but the majority of the trail was well preserved. The lookout was amazing! Worth all the effort climbing up. We met many seniors along the way, who also enjoyed themselves with no difficulties. Already recommend this route to some friends.

Lovely hike, the trails are well maintained but they are shred with bikes and horses to be aware of your surroundings.  There's lots of bugs, millions of them so bring spray and make sure you climb to the top of the stairs as the views from the top are stunning.

Fun trail with plenty of detours available. The directions lead you to a parking lot that may be full and requires payment. You might find parking along the road if you get there early enough. The start of my route is by the road and gives you plenty of choices which way to wander. Some slight challenges in spots but fun nonetheless. Plan to come back and try some of the other off shoots.

Lots of different off shoots to choose from. Great day of hiking some of the trail we took was a little challenging but enjoyable. Parking is also available on the road depending where you wish to begin the hike. There is also paid parking if you follow the directions to the parking lot.

This trail takes a LOT longer to hike through that expected. It took my group of friends about 4 hours to hike the whole trail. The view from the lookout point is outstanding and you also get to pass by a little pond. The only downfall was our poor choice of visiting a week after the April 2018 snowstorm in Ontario - all the snow was melting faster than the soil could absorb it, leaving us to trek through large amounts of very deep puddles. Despite that, it was an amazing experience and I’d love to explore it again!

It's longer than it looks. The access up is a switchback style trail and not great if you have problems climbing. Great view. Lost of different types of berries from gooseberries to blackberry and even some grapes planted years ago that flourish.
